issues.body: The new wording "W3C has published no RDF-1.2 dataset canonicalization specification" is an unqualified negative existence claim about upstream state, carried in four places, with the supporting citation removed. Two consequences: (1) a reader can no longer follow a pointer to check it, and (2) it silently goes stale the moment W3C publishes anything in this space -- including a mere Working Draft, which is still a W3C *publication*, so the sentence could become literally false while the substantive point (no normative RDF-1.2 canonicalization exists) stays true. The same file already models the better pattern about 90 lines lower: "Status checked 2026-08-01 (issue #3455): W3C rdf12-n-quads is a **Working Draft** (23 July 2026) and has never been published past Working Draft" -- dated, precise about publication maturity, and tied to a tracking issue. The old phrasing ("unsettled upstream") was weaker but robust to a WD landing; the new one is sharper but brittle. Nothing here is wrong today on the evidence available in-repo, so this is not blocking.
issues.fix_hint: Prefer maturity-precise, dated wording in the canonical spot (rdf12.rs module docs), e.g. "W3C has published no RDF-1.2 dataset canonicalization *Recommendation* (status checked 2026-08-01)", and let the shorter surfaces (Cargo.toml / README / SKILL.md / lib.rs) point at it. If the citation was dropped because it was judged a misattribution rather than merely redundant, say so in the PR body so the next reader does not re-add it.
issues.title: Undated, uncited absolute upstream-status claim replaces a cited hedge

issues.body: research/rdf-canon-rdf12-triple-terms-upstream.md (lines 15-16) still describes triple-term canonicalization as "currently **undefined** upstream ([w3c/rdf-star-wg#114])", and its item-3 draft as "not yet a stable normative reference". That file is outside this diff (hence filed against the rdf12.rs docs it mirrors). It is a dated 2026-07-17 design record, so leaving it untouched is defensible; flagging only so the inconsistency is a deliberate choice rather than an oversight.
issues.fix_hint: Either leave the research record as an explicitly point-in-time artifact (it already carries a Date: header) or add a one-line dated status update to it referencing the wording change made here.

verdict.summary: Doc-only change across crates/sparq-canon (Cargo.toml feature comment, README, lib.rs and rdf12.rs module docs) and skills/rdf-canon/SKILL.md. It replaces the hedged phrase "their canonicalization is unsettled upstream (w3c/rdf-star-wg#114)" with the flat statement "W3C has published no RDF-1.2 dataset canonicalization specification" and drops the issue citation. No Rust code, no test, no public API, no feature wiring changes: `rdf12-triple-terms = ["dep:sha2"]` is untouched, so there is no correctness, soundness, or security surface and no vacuous-test risk. Verified locally: (a) the removed reference-style link definition `[w3c/rdf-star-wg#114]:` in rdf12.rs had exactly one use, which the same hunk removes, so no dangling markdown reference / rustdoc broken-link warning is introduced (`[RDFC-1.0]` remains defined and used); (b) `scripts/check-terminology.py` on all five changed files is clean (the removed spellings were allow-listed proper nouns, the added prose contains no banned term); (c) `scripts/check-readme-template.py` reports 0 deviations across 68 READMEs; (d) the fail-closed behaviour statements the docs make (feature OFF => byte-identical, `CanonError::TripleTerm` on triple terms) are unchanged and still match the code. All four doc surfaces plus the Cargo.toml comment were updated together, so doc-sync is respected. The new claim is consistent with what the repo itself records (RDFC-1.0 is RDF-1.1-only; rdf12-n-quads is still a Working Draft per the dated status note further down rdf12.rs), and it is a narrower, more checkable statement than "unsettled upstream". Remaining remarks are non-blocking: the new claim is an undated, uncited absolute negative where the same file elsewhere dates its upstream-status assertions, one comment line wraps raggedly, and research/rdf-canon-rdf12-triple-terms-upstream.md still carries the old "undefined upstream (#114)" framing (that file is outside this diff).
